messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - Streaming API (/v1/stream/generate) experiencing token cadence stalls and elevated p99 (>2.5s) across multiple regions for ~20m. Paging @oncall-ml marta. Please ack and attach quick metrics.

marta: acked. jumping in. changing status to On Call. who rolled what recently?

devin: pushing graphs — kv_cache.per_shard bytes jumped from ~140MB -> ~1.3GB over 22m on several shards, continuous_batching observed burst windows ~900-1500ms and batch_tokens spikes up to ~25k. streaming write queue depth rising.

devin: logs snippet:```
[2026-03-03T09:12:45Z] shard=4 kv_cache.bytes=141233920
[2026-03-03T09:34:09Z] shard=4 kv_cache.bytes=1321048576 warn="evict_delay"
[2026-03-03T09:34:10Z] shard=4 continuous_batch_ms=1080 batch_tokens=24512
[2026-03-03T09:34:10Z] stream flush_event partial_flush_count=5 err="missed_timer"
```

rahul: noted. We enabled kv-prefetch for streaming routes ~3h ago (flag: streaming.kv_prefetch=on) to cut cold latency. Might have widened active cache set. Also small GC hiccups in node logs around 09:34.

marta: probable causal chain: kv-prefetch expands working set -> continuous batching accumulates very large batches -> kv cache grows -> memory pressure + GC -> flush timers miss -> token cadence stalls. Mitigation plan (immediate): 1) cap kv cache per-shard 2) reduce continuous_batching window/token cap 3) toggle off kv-prefetch on streaming route 4) canary rollout and observe.

marta: running hotfix now:```bash
# per-shard cap to 300MB
infractl config set runtime.kv_cache.max_bytes_per_shard=314572800 --env prod --target streaming-pool
# lower batching latency window and token cap
infractl config set runtime.continuous_batching.max_wait_ms=40 --env prod --target streaming-pool
infractl config set runtime.continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens=512 --env prod --target streaming-pool
# disable streaming prefetch
infractl config set models.streaming_route.kv_prefetch=false --env prod --target streaming-pool
```

opsbot: initiating canary rollout (15%) for change cfg-20260303-002. Applying configs: runtime.kv_cache.max_bytes_per_shard=314572800, runtime.continuous_batching.max_wait_ms=40, runtime.continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens=512, models.streaming_route.kv_prefetch=false

opsbot: canary at 15% healthy after 90s. p99 reduced from ~2.8s -> 0.6s on canary nodes. no partial_flush errors on canary. increasing to 60%.

devin: observing canary metrics — per-shard cache stabilized ~280-305MB, batch_tokens capped around 480, continuous_batch window ~30-40ms. partial flush events dropped to zero on canary.

opsbot: rollout to 100% complete at t+26m. change cfg-20260303-002 status=success :white_check_mark:

marta: mitigation effective. overall p99 back to ~0.55s and streaming queues drained. Still seeing scattered "partial_flush_count" logs (~1-2/min) on a small fraction of connections — looks like a separate race in the streaming flush path when timers are aggressive. Filed runtime issue: https://stash.internal/redwood/runtime/issues/4392

rahul: extra context: prefetch was safe in normal batch sizes but exposed worst-case when combined with continuous batching configs we had. We'll keep prefetch off for streaming until we add safeguards (cache hard caps + prefetch admission control).

marta: handoff to liz for next shift. summary for post-incident: cause=kv-prefetch + permissive continuous batching -> kv cache blowup -> GC/memory pressure -> missed flush timers -> token cadence stalls. mitigation=cfg-20260303-002 (caps + lower window + disable prefetch). follow-ups: 1) postmortem doc + timeline 2) add e2e test for partial flush under small windows 3) add alert: kv_cache.per_shard > 400MB for >4m 4) revisit prefetch rollout plan with admission controls 5) customer comms. dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streaming/streaming-overview ; logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/q?k=partial_flush

liz: taking over. I'll coordinate the postmortem and assign owners. thanks for the handoff @marta.

csm-naomi: customer impact brief: support intake shows 7 customers reported degraded streaming (stuttering / delayed tokens). 3 customers opened support tickets for truncated or incomplete streams (IDs: TKT-9011, TKT-9013, TKT-9018). I'll draft outreach + credits and post affected customers list in #customer-impact.

marta: ok locking channel to ops only. If regressions reappear we will re-open paging. Great work team.

incident-bot: Incident P1 -> mitigated. Required follow-ups: create postmortem in #incidents-postmortems, tag @eng-runtime @oncall-ml @csm-naomi.
